harnesses.bounds: every budget record, change and dead rule at full width; no loop
assumptions: the dead rule is one of its three values
the lock effects are empty stubs; budget_step takes no lock

harnesses.bounds: chains of CHAIN_DEPTH budgets starting at the leaf, counters at most CHAIN_VALUE_MAX, any 64-bit change; loops unwound 5 times
assumptions: the chain has the shape erx_budget_carve and erx_budget_init_root make: parent links, depths, a cap at or above the guarantee and equal to it for a wall, a live wall root of at most INT64_MAX pages
counters at most CHAIN_VALUE_MAX: the full-width arithmetic of one level is budget_step's and budget_arith's harness
the ticket lock is a stub that checks its own use; one thread
unsupported: chains deeper than CHAIN_DEPTH, up to ERX_BUDGET_DEPTH_MAX = 16: the solver's cost grows with each level

harnesses.bounds: every resting count and generation within the ABI bounds, zero to two opening writes, a clear or a release; the opening loop unwound 3 times
assumptions: the slot rests at an even count of at most CAP_SEQ_FREE_MAX and a generation below CAP_GENERATION_LIMIT; the harness proves the closing write hands both on
one thread: each _Atomic access is indivisible and sequentially consistent, its memory order ignored (test/cbmc/include/stdatomic.h)
unsupported: _Atomic loads and stores with explicit memory orders: modelled as sequentially consistent, through __atomic builtins, since CBMC does not know clang's __c11_atomic builtins

harnesses.bounds: tables of 2 to 128 slots with one page of 64 added, one slot of the page in any quiescent state, every value, reader, type and rights; the sequence-count loop unwound twice
assumptions: the slot read is quiescent, its count even or terminal: with one thread an odd count would spin the loop for ever
one thread: each _Atomic access is indivisible and sequentially consistent, its memory order ignored (test/cbmc/include/stdatomic.h)
unsupported: the sequence-count retry loop of cap_read_slot under a concurrent writer: unbounded by design, and CBMC's interleavings have no fairness, so only the quiescent read is checked
_Atomic loads and stores with explicit memory orders: modelled as sequentially consistent, through __atomic builtins, since CBMC does not know clang's __c11_atomic builtins

harnesses.bounds: every request of up to ERX_MSG_CAPS = 4 items, every source view; loops unwound 6 times
assumptions: the sources are free, a superset of what erx_cap_read returns under the locks

harnesses.bounds: any tracker state the record invariant allows, at full width over all 64 CPU bits; one retirement then GRACE_STEPS = 4 joins, leaves, reports or retirements of any CPU; settle unwound 3 times
assumptions: the callers keep the tracker's contract: a CPU below ERX_CPUSET_BITS, and a retirement with a CPU online and room for the next count
the lock effect is a stub that checks its own pairing; one thread
unsupported: more than GRACE_STEPS calls after the retirement: the start from any invariant state covers every reachable state, but a stamp's whole life is checked only over GRACE_STEPS calls
progress: that a stamp does mature once every owed CPU has reported is a liveness property, which the host tests check and this harness does not

harnesses.bounds: FUNNEL_PAGES = 4 page records; FUNNEL_STEPS = 5 calls among charge, backing step, take, release, reaper's free and the end of grace periods; loops unwound 6 times
assumptions: the grace tracker is a stub of erx/grace.h's contract: a retirement stamps the next count and a stamp matures once the completed count reaches it; the grace_tracker harness checks the tracker itself
the budget core's reserve steps are stubs that keep erx/budget.h's contract for one reserve, admitting at most the pages that exist: the identity the budget core keeps for the machine
the page allocator is a stub over the harness's free list that hands out the request, or every free page when fewer are free
one backing at a time; the lock effects are stubs that check their pairing and the owner-before-list order; one thread
unsupported: a second CPU running the funnel at once: the order that keeps a refund after its pages' append (the identity's inequality under concurrency) is not a single-thread property
the budget core's own reserve steps: budget_step and budget_chain check those

harnesses.bounds: one table of one page and two objects; SLOT_STEPS = 2 installs of a kind, copies, clears or closes with every mask and object, and values naming slots 0 to SLOT_STEPS + 1 at generation 0 or 1; then one lookup; loops unwound 6 times, the page's set-up 65
assumptions: one thread holding the locks the writers name: each _Atomic access is indivisible and sequentially consistent, its memory order ignored (test/cbmc/include/stdatomic.h)
the object store and the attach insert are stubs that keep erx/object.h's and erx/attach.h's contracts; the budget's death is a stub returning a value chosen at random and fixed for the run
unsupported: a lookup racing a writer: the sequence-count retry is cap_read's quiescent check and the host race tests
a clear of a slot with a neighbour on its list: the one clear two calls allow follows one install, so the neighbour branches of erx_cap_slot_clear never run; the host model and cap_fuzz.c cover them
more than SLOT_STEPS calls, other values or a second table: each object's list is checked over the slots SLOT_STEPS installs can reach, and every other value is cap_read's harness
